summary: Most reviewers like the rechargeable battery, which lets them pump around the house, in the car or on a road trip, and many say the strong suction empties them better than wearables. The main downside is that it is heavy and bulky, so it is not very discreet or easy to bring to work. Suits those who pump mostly at home.

Most reviewers call the Vista V2 sturdy and smooth to push, with a big basket and capable on snow, gravel and cobblestones. The main downside is size: it is bulky and takes up a lot of trunk space. As a double, a growing toddler can outgrow the rumble seat, and the extra seat and adapters add cost.

Reviews are split. Many say output matches or nearly matches a Spectra and praise the freedom to move around and the comfort. Others find it finicky, with membranes and cups that must be aligned just right or suction is lost, plus quality problems such as motor failures and leaks. It is also heavy and bulky for some.

Most reviewers value the hands-free freedom to pump while moving around, travelling or caring for other kids. The main complaint is low output: several say it does not empty them like a Spectra, so it works better as a convenient extra than a powerful primary pump. A few also hit reliability problems.

Most reviewers love it as a light, compact stroller with a quick one-handed fold, and many use it for frequent flying. Downsides are a small basket, a flimsy feel for some, and it takes two hands to open. Several say it suits travel and city life better than rougher everyday use.

Many reviewers like the reliable app, remote viewing and the breathing band for peace of mind with a newborn. The main complaints are the subscription needed for history and extras and the high price for what is otherwise a camera. Some also mention occasional connection drops or needing to re-pair WiFi.

Reviewers are very positive about this light, compact travel stroller with a one-handed fold, and many say it feels sturdy and holds up to hard use. A few note it is rough on uneven sidewalks and some find it less sturdy than hoped. Many use it for flights and daily errands alongside a bigger stroller.

Reviewers are split. Many say it eased their anxiety and helped them sleep, with no or very few false alarms. Others got frequent false alarms from lost connections or a loose sock and stopped using it. Suits anxious parents, though false alarms are the main risk.

Most reviewers like this cheap high chair for being very easy to wipe clean, light and simple to assemble. The main complaints are that it is bulky with legs that stick out and can trip people, and that the tray is hard to remove. Some also dislike the harness and the lack of a footrest.

Most reviewers find it quick and easy to put on and good for newborns. The main downside is that many outgrow it within a few months, finding the stretchy fabric unsupportive as the baby gets heavier, and a few report back pain. It suits short use with a small baby.

Most reviewers say the strong suction empties them about as well as or better than a Spectra or wall pump, and like pumping hands-free. Complaints are few: one found it could not keep up after returning to work, and one said the motor weakened after several months.

Most reviewers like it as a good value, easy-to-use stroller that folds with one hand and lasts for years. The main downside is a bumpy, wobbly ride off smooth pavement, and some found it flimsy and moved to a pricier stroller. Suits those wanting a budget travel system.

Most reviewers say their breastfed baby would take these when other bottles were refused, and describe an easy switch between breast and bottle and a good latch. They are also easy to clean with few parts. A couple found the flow too fast, and one had bags that leaked.

Reviewers liked tracking breathing without anything on the baby, but the main complaint is that features were moved behind a paid subscription after purchase, which left many angry. Some also report a glitchy app, connection drops and trouble on Android.

Most reviewers find it very easy to clean and assemble, light, and easy to pack up for travel. The main complaints are a small tray and wide legs that are a tripping hazard. Some also wanted a more adjustable footrest.

Reviewers like the sturdy, good-looking wooden chair that grows with the child and fits under the table. The main complaint is cleaning, especially the straps, tray and nooks that trap food, and the straps are also hard to adjust. Opinion is split, with some happy to buy a second.

Most reviewers use it to catch letdown from the breast not being fed from, and many built a freezer stash that way without pumping. It is easy to wash. A few found it in the way or yielded very little, and one linked its continuous suction to oversupply and mastitis.

Most reviewers like the strong suction and freedom of a wearable, and several say it matches a Spectra. The main complaint is durability: motors failed within months for several, though customer service usually replaced them. A few found it painful or low in output.

Reviewers love the smooth, one-handed rotating seat that makes loading a child much easier, especially for shorter parents. Many say it fits smaller cars fairly well, and it feels solid. A couple of drawbacks: it is deep and can eat front-seat legroom, and one chest clip was faulty but replaced quickly.

Most reviewers like how easy it is to clean, with few parts and room to reach inside by hand. Some babies would not take it or had a flow they disliked, and a few found it leaked or tipped over easily because of the small base.

Most reviewers end up happy with the Ergobaby Omni Classic, finding it comfortable for the parent and usable well past the baby stage. Its main downsides are a newborn fit that often needs an insert or a few months of waiting, and clips or a fit that make putting it on alone tricky.

Most reviewers love how smoothly the Nuna MIXX next rides, with big wheels and suspension that cope with gravel, cobblestones and uneven sidewalks. Some find it heavy and bulky, and one had trouble folding it. A few say it sits unused once life gets less urban.

Most reviewers find the Chicco KeyFit 35 easy to install and use, and several reused it for a second child or paired it with a stroller. The main downside is weight, especially with a growing baby in it. One found the baby too hot and switched early to a convertible seat.

Most reviewers find the UPPAbaby Cruz V2 sturdy and worth the splurge, handling uneven surfaces and offering a big basket. The main downsides are weight and bulk, and a few say it is hard to fit in a trunk or too much to travel with. Suits daily use more than flights.

Most reviewers praise the easy ClickTight install on the Britax One4Life ClickTight, including moving it between cars. The main downsides are its weight and size, and a couple found the harness very hard to tighten, one returning it for that.

Reviewers consistently love the Bugaboo Butterfly 2 as a travel stroller, folding easily with one hand and fitting in small cars and on planes. Several also use it as an everyday stroller. Small downsides are small wheels catching on tracks, a recline that could be flatter, and uncertainty about airline size rules.

Reviewers are split on the Happiest Baby SNOO. Those whose babies took to it say it helps them sleep and stay asleep, and would buy it again. Others found the baby hated the motion, the white noise too loud, or saw no sleep improvement. Several suggest renting or buying used first.

Most reviewers love how light and easy to fold the Nuna TRIV next is, using it as a single everyday stroller that fits well in the car. Downsides are a smaller basket and a less smooth ride than bigger strollers. One reported a car seat that wobbled on the stroller.

Most reviewers love the Doona Car Seat & Stroller for travel and convenience, popping open from car seat to stroller for flights, taxis and trips. Downsides are that it gets heavy to lift as the baby grows, and it lacks storage and is less comfortable to push on rough ground. Many call it worth the splurge.

Most reviewers love the swivel on the Cybex Sirona S, which makes getting a baby in and out of the car easier. The main downside is installation, which some found finicky or wobbly. A few add that it is large and hefty, and the rotation stops once forward-facing.

Reviewers love the rotating seat on the Graco Turn2Me 3-in-1, which makes buckling a baby or toddler in far easier, even a fussy one. Some say it fits small cars well. Limits mentioned are that it only rotates rear-facing, takes a lot of room, and one child reached the rear-facing limit.

Reviews of the Halo BassiNest Swivel Sleeper 4.0 are mixed. Some babies sleep well in it, especially as newborns, and one reports it lasting through several babies. Several babies rejected it, and some found the base large, with legs that would not slide under the bed. Some outgrow it early.

Most reviewers love the Solly Baby Wrap for the newborn months, finding it cozy and comfortable to wear for hours. The downsides are that it is tricky to wrap correctly and gets hot or less useful as the baby grows. It suits the early weeks and months best.

Most reviewers like the Spectra S2 Plus, finding it effective, customizable and more comfortable than some alternatives. The main complaint is being tied to a wall outlet, which some fix with a battery pack. A few found it bulky, loud or a lot to clean, and one pump stopped working within weeks.

Reviewers are split on the Artipoppe Zeitgeist Baby Carrier. Those it suits find it the most comfortable carrier, with a wide waistband that carries weight for hours and works into toddlerhood. Others found it bulky, hot or uncomfortable even after expert help, and said it was not worth the price.

Most reviewers like the BabyBjörn Baby Carrier Mini for newborns, since it is quick and easy to put on and take off alone. The main downside is back strain for the parent, so it suits short wears more than long ones. Several babies loved it and used it for months.

Reviewers are generally positive about the Britax Boulevard ClickTight, often praising its easy install and secure feel, though one says the ClickTight is tricky at first. Downsides are that it is bulky and heavy, and some found the harness hard to adjust or tighten. A few switched to another brand.

Most reviewers like the Chicco KeyFit 30 as a reliable, easy seat that clicks in and out of cars and strollers. The main downside is weight once the baby grows, which led some to carry it less or move on early. A couple of babies disliked sitting in it.

Reviewers love how smoothly the Cybex Gazelle S glides, including on grass, dirt roads and trails, and like its big storage and single-to-double options. The one downside is a fold that can stick or feel stiff at first. Many call it worth the money.

Most reviewers like the Infant Optics DXR-8 as a simple non-WiFi monitor with no app or subscription and a battery that lasts the night. The main downside is that the connection can drop at a distance, such as in the garage or basement. Some call the picture and screen basic, but several say it lasts for years.

Most reviewers love the UPPAbaby Mesa V2, finding it easy to use and carry, with an insert that fits newborns well and a simple click into stroller or car. Some babies disliked it, one turning red, and one found a convertible more comfortable. Suits families who want an infant seat for stroller use and road trips.
